subject: mathematics
question_text: Find a vector in the direction of the vector a = i − 2j that has magnitude 7 units.

recall_prompt: Say how you would build a vector of a given length in a given direction.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the unit vector
steps.margin_note: First mark. Same opening as any direction question: get the length, then divide to get the unit vector. Note a lies in the xy-plane, so there is no k term.

recall.must_convey: That |a| = √5 and the unit vector in the direction of a is (i − 2j)/√5.
accept: the magnitude is root five so the unit vector is i minus two j over root five
find mod a which is root five then divide
get the unit vector first by dividing by root five
magnitude root five, unit vector i minus two j by root five
first the unit vector in that direction

steps.why: A vector of any length in a direction is that length times the unit vector, so the unit vector is the piece worth building first.
common_mistakes: Adding a k component that is not there.

steps.label: Multiply by 7
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Length times direction: 7 times the unit vector has length exactly 7 and points the same way.
lines: A vector of magnitude 7 in this direction is

recall.must_convey: That multiplying the unit vector by 7 gives a vector of magnitude 7 in the same direction.
accept: multiply the unit vector by seven to get seven times i minus two j over root five
seven times the unit vector gives magnitude seven
scale the unit vector up by seven
unit vector ni seven tho multiply cheyyali
the answer is seven into i minus two j by root five

steps.why: Multiplying by a positive number changes only the length, never the direction — which is why this construction gives the right direction automatically.
common_mistakes: Multiplying the original vector by 7 without dividing by √5 first.
